description: ODC: delete a BLOCK that already existed. Nothing is born here: the `base` is job:block-reuse, and this job opens a module that ALREADY HAS WfCovPriceTag instantiated 3 times and WfCovPolicyCard instantiated 2, in different screens. The only thing it does is take that apart in the right order, with `usages` proving each step. The order is not creation in reverse: the instances go from TOP to bottom (the screen consumes the middle block, the middle block consumes the bottom one), and each `delete` only passes without `force` after the target is at zero. THE CORE: when the middle block goes, the `usages` of WfCovPriceTag falls from 3 to 1 without anyone touching it - two of its instances lived INSIDE WfCovPolicyCard and went with it, because the delete takes the whole tree. Whoever tries to delete the bottom block first gets the refusal that names the 3 consumers; whoever deletes the top one first does not even need to know they existed. One instance is left by hand, the one that was born from the HTML fragment in WfCovPolicySummary, and only then does WfCovPriceTag go without force. WHAT DOES NOT GO ON ITS OWN: the delete sweeps down and never up, so the screen variables that only served to feed the arguments (PolicyLabel, RenewalPremium) stay alive and orphaned - whoever counts on automatic cleanup leaves the module full of dead variables, and that is why they go here with `usages` at zero proving no one reads them any more. The placeholder content proves the other side: the Quote was read by the note inside the visual instance, and its `usages` falls to zero with the delete of the INSTANCE, without touching the note - that note belongs to the consumer and not to the block, as job:block-reuse shows when creating it. Exact pair: tests/jobs-odc/block-reuse.json assembles, this one disassembles; the corresponding refusal (delete of a block with a live instance) is proven in the O11 lane in tests/jobs-negative/delete-block-in-use.json, and the clean path for logic and data in the ODC lane itself in tests/jobs-odc/delete-logic-consumers.json and delete-data-consumers.json.

ops._why: STARTING POINT, all inherited: 3 instances of the bottom block, in TWO different parents - two inside IMobileBlock:WfCovPolicyCard and one inside IMobileScreen:WfCovPolicySummary. None of them goes on its own.
the MIDDLE block: 2 instances, one in each screen. It is a consumer of the bottom one and consumed by the screens at the same time - and it is the one that decides the order.

the screen variable before touching anything: 1 reader. And note WHO the usages names: it is not the IArgument, it is the ITextBasedExpression INSIDE it - the argument is the box, the expression is what reads, and that is why the reader dies together with the instance that hosts it. Keep the 1: this is the variable that will be left orphaned, not deleted.
(1a) TOP FIRST: the instance in the screen is the topmost consumer. The screen survives, it only loses the widget.
(1b) the second instance of the SAME block, in the other screen: two instances with the same name, two distinct deletes, because the name belongs to the PARENT
(2) zero: the middle block was left without instances and its delete already passes without force
(3) STILL 3: deleting the instances of the middle block did not touch a single instance of the bottom one. The two inside are still alive because WfCovPolicyCard is still alive.
(4) the middle block goes without force - and takes the whole body with it, including the two WfCovPriceTag instances that were inside

(5) THE CORE OF THE PROOF: it fell from 3 to 1 without a single operation on WfCovPriceTag or on its instances. The delete sweeps the tree downward, and the count of what the target CONSUMED changes in its wake. What remains is the visual instance in WfCovPolicySummary, which was not inside anything deleted.

ops.name: WfCovPolicyCard
ops._why: (5) the middle block no longer exists: empty list
(6) before deleting the last instance: the variable feeds its Amount argument
(6) and this one is read by the NOTE inside the placeholder of the instance - content that belongs to the consumer, not to the block

(7a) the third instance before it goes. Note the PATH: it is by DESCENDANT (`**`), not by child - the HTML fragment hangs the instance inside an IContent of the container, and the direct child of WfCovSummaryBoard is that IContent. Whoever writes the path as if the `<Block>` were a child of the `<div>` gets a KeyNotFoundException with the list of the real children.

(7b) the third instance, the one that was born from the HTML fragment: this one is by hand, because it did not live inside anything that was deleted. The container WfCovSummaryBoard stays, with the title that was not the block's.

(8) zero without touching the note: it was inside the IPlaceholderContentWidget:Footnote of the INSTANCE (the path in the previous usages shows it in full) and went with it. Proof from the opposite side of what job:block-reuse shows when creating it: the placeholder content belongs to the consumer.
(9) zero: now, yes, the bottom block has no consumers
(10) THE REQUEST: the inherited block goes without force, because the 3 instances have already gone - two in its wake, one by hand

ops.name: WfCovPriceTag
ops._why: (10) empty list: neither block nor instance remained

(11) WHAT DID NOT GO ON ITS OWN: the variable started with 1 reader, is at zero and is still on the screen. The delete never goes up: whoever only looks at the block leaves the module with dead variables.
(11) so it goes here, with the usages at zero authorizing it
(12) the same thing on the other screen: it was read by the expression RenewalPremium * 1.15 of the argument, and the expression went with the instance
READ BACK: the screen is still whole - same name, same theme, same layout - and now with LocalVariables=0, which is the cleanup of step (11) showing up in the properties and not only in the usages
MainContent empty: no instance or dangling argument remained
the fragment container survived with its title; what belonged to the block disappeared entirely
what remains of blocks in the module: those from the library, neither of the two authored
